author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Christian Harrison and Neal Skupski won the U.S. Open men’s doubles championship on Saturday, defeating Germany’s Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz 6-4, 7-6 (6). The title gave the American-British partnership its second Grand Slam trophy of the season after winning the Australian Open.

Harrison and Skupski controlled the opening set, then closed a tighter second set in a tiebreak. Their ability to finish in straight sets limited the opportunity for Krawietz and Puetz to force a deciding third set on the New York hard courts.

The victory completes a notable two-major season for a pairing that has translated complementary serving and net play into results on different surfaces and continents. Grand Slam doubles matches often turn on a small number of return points and quick exchanges, making the second-set tiebreak the decisive pressure moment. Harrison and Skupski handled it to secure the championship without extending the match. The result also places them among the season’s most successful men’s doubles teams, with major titles at both the first and final Grand Slam events of 2026.
dek: The American-British pair beat Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz in straight sets for its second major title of 2026.
headline: Harrison and Skupski win U.S. Open men’s doubles title
